A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GroundingBooth and have readable text, equations, tables and figures that support comparison. v1 ends with references; v3 includes readable Appendices A-K.

before.justification: v1 reports original DreamBench and COCO experiments, component ablations in Tables 1-4, and qualitative single- and multi-subject generation results.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations, quantitative multi-subject comparisons, a user study, and additional qualitative investigations in its appendices.

M1.justification: The overall grounding architecture remains. The stated attention procedure changes from multiplicative masking of logits and output in v1 Eqs. 7-8 to additive zero/negative-infinity masking of logits without the final output mask in v3 Eqs. 4-5. This establishes a localized revision to the described computation, without establishing implementation changes.

E1.justification: v3 adds Refer-YouTube-VOS object videos and segmented OpenImages v7 images to the stated MVImgNet/LVIS training mix. Appendix evaluations add zero-layout and absent-reference input scenarios, explicit action/pose cases, and object interactions. DreamBench, COCO and multi-subject customization remain covered.

E2.justification: The DreamBench table removes SD v1.4 and adds MS-Diffusion. The COCO comparison adds UniControl and InstanceDiffusion alongside the retained LAMA, LayoutDiffusion and GLIGEN. v3 also introduces quantitative multi-subject comparisons against lambda-eclipse and MS-Diffusion, substantially expanding evaluated competition.

E3.justification: v3 adds COCO FID and YOLOv8-based AP/AP50 evaluation. Its new quantitative multi-subject protocol randomly pairs DreamBench subjects and averages per-subject identity scores into M-CLIP-I/M-DINO. A new paired user study uses random layouts, 30 objects, 25 prompts, over 530 users and more than 1,200 votes.

E4.justification: The original grounding-module and attention-removal ablations remain, with additional COCO evaluation metrics. Appendices E-H add qualitative investigations of bounding-box shape versus pose, removal of grounding/reference conditions, object interaction, and action-prompt following, including comparisons in Figure 12.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new user-study participant and vote counts describe sample size rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: GroundingBooth's reported DreamBench CLIP-T/CLIP-I/DINO scores change from 0.2881/0.9146/0.7884 to 0.2931/0.9169/0.7950; ELITE, lambda-eclipse and AnyDoor entries also change. COCO and full-model ablation scores are revised. New results include multi-subject comparisons, user preferences, and COCO FID/AP/AP50 of 25.63/37.4/52.6 for GroundingBooth. Expanded training coverage and incomplete protocol correspondence prevent interpreting these revisions as controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v3 substantively revises the formal mask definition and attention equation, replacing v1's multiplicative formulation with additive masking. The standard diffusion objective is retained in Appendix A after relocation. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain joint foreground/background grounding, identity preservation and multi-subject customization. v3 removes v1's explicit 'first work' and 'first attempt' novelty assertions, narrowing its stated priority claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds an interpretation that large, centered subjects can inflate identity-similarity scores, explains pose adaptation through bounding-box shape and background harmonization, and discusses behavior under missing conditions. Appendix J adds previously absent limitations concerning base-model capability and the inference cost of sequential subject integration.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly discloses four A100 GPUs, 100,000 training steps, batch size 14, learning rate 5e-5, 10% image/text embedding dropout and guidance scale 3. Missing-input handling and SAM-based preprocessing are also documented more explicitly. Conversely, v3 omits v1 Table 2's explicit COCO fine-tuning and filtered 3,097-image evaluation details; this omission does not establish a changed protocol.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused distinctions from Break-A-Scene and concurrent MS-Diffusion, emphasizing full-image and background grounding. It also adds LayoutGPT/LayoutLLM-T2I and citations supporting new experimental resources, while removing SAM2. The principal literature categories and overall positioning remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Masked cross-attention becomes subject-grounded cross-attention, the preliminary section moves to Appendix A, and experiments are reorganized around single-subject, multi-subject and complex-layout evaluation, with additional appendix sections.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the pipeline and attention diagrams, and revises the qualitative comparison panels and comparator columns. It adds multi-subject and user-study tables, expands COCO tables with additional metrics, and introduces Figures 8-13. Some existing examples are relocated rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important validation gaps: v1 supported grounding primarily through examples and similarity metrics, and multi-subject generation only qualitatively. Detection-based grounding evaluation, quantitative multi-subject comparisons and a documented user study provide substantially stronger evidence. Essential training settings and specific limitations also improve reproducibility and interpretation. Unexplained score revisions, absent uncertainty estimates and lost COCO setup details remain weaknesses, but the targeted validation and documentation provide a substantial net improvement.
